title: Formal model
description: "An appendix: what a studyflow is as a typed graph, so the claims elsewhere can be checked."
---

This page is an appendix, stating what a studyflow is so the claims made elsewhere in these docs can be checked.

There is no single specification document. The specification is spread across three pages, one per question:

| The question | Where it is answered |
|---|---|
| **What is a studyflow?** The diagram as a graph, how research meaning layers over BPMN, and what makes one well formed | this page |
| **What happens when one runs?** One participant, or one pipeline, walking the diagram | [Execution](../run/execution.qmd) |
| **How is one stored?** The `.studyflow.yaml` file, the BPMN 2.0 XML export, and images that carry the study | [File format](file-format.qmd) |

What may be *in* a studyflow is catalogued separately in [Elements](elements.qmd) and [Data](data.qmd), because that list grows whenever a new element set ships — without the notation itself changing.

A studyflow is a single object: a typed graph, in which every node and every edge carries both a type and a set of attributes. Everything the tools do is an operation over that one object.

| The tools do this | Which is, over the object | Where it happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Validate** | conditions the graph must satisfy | the modeler as you draw; `studyflow validate` in the CLI |
| **Project** | a sub-graph picked out by a predicate | the modeler's views; PNG and SVG export |
| **Execute** | a walk along the control edges, reading and writing the data nodes | the browser runner; the Python runner |

## The object

$$S = (N,\ E,\ \mathit{src},\ \mathit{tgt},\ \tau,\ \lambda)$$

$N$ is a finite set of nodes and $E$ a finite set of edges. $\mathit{src}$ and $\mathit{tgt}$ map each edge to its two endpoints. Because they are functions on edges rather than a relation on nodes, two distinct edges may join the same pair — $S$ is a multigraph.

$\tau$ assigns every node and edge its type, and $\lambda$ its attributes.

Data elements are nodes like any other. Steps and data therefore share a single node set, and only the type of the edge distinguishes control from data.

| Edge | Ends it may join | What it carries |
|---|---|---|
| `bpmn:SequenceFlow` | flow node → flow node | control: what happens next, under an optional `conditionExpression` |
| `bpmn:DataInputAssociation`, `bpmn:DataOutputAssociation` | data node ↔ an activity's port | one value in or out of a step, under an optional `transformation` binding |
| `bpmn:MessageFlow` | participant ↔ participant | an exchange between two parties |

## Types come in layers

Every element is a BPMN 2.0 element first. That is what fixes its shape and how the path moves through it. The research vocabulary is layered on top of that base, which is why a generic BPMN tool can still read the file.

| Layer | Where it is written | Example |
|---|---|---|
| the process element | the element itself | `bpmn:Task` |
| the research type it stands for | a wrapper inside `extensionElements` | `cognitive:Questionnaire` on that task |
| one attribute added to a whole family of elements | a namespaced attribute on the element | `studyflow:consentFormUri` on a start event |

## Well-formedness

| # | Condition | Enforced by |
|:--|---|---|
| 1 | Every element carries an identifier unique within the file; the canonical YAML keys each collection by id, so a repeated id has no canonical form | construction — the modeler will not draw what the notation forbids |
| 2 | Both ends of every edge resolve to declared nodes, and a sequence flow's two ends sit in the same container — one process or one sub-process | construction |
| 3 | Every container has an entry: a start event, or — for the browser runner's root process only — the single node that nothing flows into | construction |
| 4 | Sequence flows join flow nodes only, so a data node is reached through data associations alone | construction |
| 5 | Every type $\tau$ assigns is declared by a loaded schema, and an attribute no schema declares is kept verbatim and reported, never dropped | `studyflow validate` |
| 6 | A gateway with several outgoing flows needs a rule that picks one — a condition per branch with one marked `default`, or a type that declares how it branches, such as `cognitive:RandomGateway` | the two runners, row by row in [Execution](../run/execution.qmd) |
| 7 | Every attribute value belongs to the type its schema declares, enumerations included (`runtime` is `browser`, `cloud`, `local`, or `hpc`) | `studyflow validate` |

## Projections

A view is a predicate. Given a predicate $P$ over nodes and edges, the view is $S_P$: those elements satisfying $P$, carrying their types and attributes exactly as $S$ has them.

| View | Keeps the nodes carrying |
|---|---|
| Timeline | `onset`, `duration`, or `progress` |
| Checklist | a `studyflow:checklist` documentation entry |
| Provenance | `prov:Activity` entries, on the study and on any element with its own |

A projection can only discard. None renames an element, rewrites a type, or computes an attribute that $S$ does not already hold.

Since $S_P \subseteq S$, a view can be incomplete but never inconsistent with the file it came from. This is the property that makes a figure exported from a studyflow evidence rather than illustration.

## The grammar

The canonical `.studyflow.yaml` is read against the schemas the tools load, and [Elements](elements.qmd#the-seven-element-sets) lists the types with their attributes.

```ebnf
/* ========== Top level ========== */
Definitions   ::= (Study | Collaboration)+
Study         ::= 'studyflow:Study' Identifier Attribute* Provenance? (Node | Edge)*
                                              /* runtime, seed, version, authors, tags */
Collaboration ::= 'bpmn:Collaboration' Identifier Pool+ Edge*
Pool          ::= 'bpmn:Participant' Identifier ('@type' PoolType)? Attribute*
PoolType      ::= 'cognitive:Actor' | 'eeg:Session'

/* ========== Nodes ========== */
Node          ::= Event | Activity | Gateway | DataNode | Container
Container     ::= ('bpmn:SubProcess' | 'bpmn:AdHocSubProcess') Identifier
                  ('@type' 'agentic:Agent')? Attribute* (Node | Edge)*

Event         ::= EventKind Identifier Attribute*
EventKind     ::= 'bpmn:StartEvent'               /* consentFormUri */
                | 'bpmn:IntermediateCatchEvent'   /* timer delay, conditional sensor */
                | 'bpmn:IntermediateThrowEvent'
                | 'bpmn:EndEvent'                 /* redirectTo, completionCodeType, completionCode */

/* Which process element a research type may sit on is fixed by the schema declaring it. */
Activity      ::= ActivityKind Identifier ('@type' ActivityType)? Attribute*
ActivityKind  ::= 'bpmn:Task' | 'bpmn:UserTask' | 'bpmn:ServiceTask' | 'bpmn:ScriptTask'
                | 'bpmn:ManualTask' | 'bpmn:ChoreographyTask'
ActivityType  ::= 'cognitive:CognitiveTask' | 'cognitive:Questionnaire'
                | 'cognitive:Instruction' | 'cognitive:Rest' | 'cognitive:BehaverseTask'
                | 'functional:Transform' | 'functional:Map'
                | 'functional:Reduce' | 'functional:Filter'
                | 'agentic:LLMCall' | 'agentic:Tool' | 'agentic:HumanApproval'

Gateway       ::= GatewayKind Identifier ('@type' GatewayType)? Attribute*
GatewayKind   ::= 'bpmn:ExclusiveGateway' | 'bpmn:InclusiveGateway' | 'bpmn:ParallelGateway'
                | 'bpmn:ComplexGateway' | 'bpmn:EventBasedGateway'
GatewayType   ::= 'cognitive:RandomGateway'      /* stratified allocation = this + stratifyBy */
                | 'cognitive:EligibilityGateway'
                | 'agentic:Router'               /* model-driven branching */

/* ========== Data nodes ========== */
DataNode      ::= DataKind Identifier Attribute*          /* uri, format, schema */
DataKind      ::= 'bpmn:DataObjectReference' | 'bpmn:DataStoreReference'
                | 'studyflow:Dataset' | 'studyflow:Schema' | 'studyflow:Table'
                | 'studyflow:Timeseries' | 'studyflow:EventMarker' | 'studyflow:Parameters'
                | 'agentic:Prompt' | 'agentic:Memory' | 'eeg:Recording'
/* studyflow:DataCatalog is not drawn: a dataset names it through its `catalog`. */

/* ========== Edges ========== */
Edge            ::= SequenceFlow | DataAssociation | MessageFlow
SequenceFlow    ::= 'bpmn:SequenceFlow' Identifier NodeRef '->' NodeRef Attribute*
                                              /* conditionExpression, default */
DataAssociation ::= ('bpmn:DataInputAssociation' | 'bpmn:DataOutputAssociation')
                    Identifier NodeRef '->' NodeRef Binding?
Binding         ::= 'transformation' (Slot ('=' Selection)? | Selection)
MessageFlow     ::= 'bpmn:MessageFlow' Identifier NodeRef '->' NodeRef Attribute*

/* ========== Provenance: append-only, oldest first ========== */
Provenance    ::= ('prov:Activity' Attribute*)+
                                              /* action, when, who, with, what, run, seed, note */

/* ========== Common ========== */
Attribute     ::= Identifier Value
NodeRef       ::= Identifier
Slot          ::= Identifier | 'self' | '*'
Selection     ::= String
Value         ::= String | Number | Boolean | Identifier
Boolean       ::= 'true' | 'false'
Number        ::= '-'? ( [0-9]+ ('.' [0-9]*)? | '.' [0-9]+ )
String        ::= '"' [^"]* '"'
Identifier    ::= [A-Za-z] [A-Za-z0-9_]*
```

Four vocabularies are always available: `studyflow`, `prov`, `functional`, and `cognitive`. The optional `agentic` and `eeg` vocabularies add further types in the same slots. `ml` adds no types at all — it ships ready-made steps you drag onto the canvas.
